title: "GSEA: permutation versus rotation"

# limit to 80 works per line
GSEA tests whether a set of genes is enriched in a ranked list of genes. The
ranking is typically based on a test statistic, such as the t-statistic from a
differential expression analysis. To assess the significance of the enrichment,
GSEA can use either permutation or rotation methods.

Rotations methods create a null distribution of the test statistic by
randomising the error in the model, while keeping the design matrix fixed.
This is particularly useful when the sample size is small, as it allows for more
accurate estimation of the null distribution. Each randomisation is a new
realisation of the data, and the test statistic is recalculated for each
randomisation.

The correlation between any two given genes will be identical in each randomisation,
as the design matrix is fixed.
